tour_info.title: from sharm elsheikh the lost city petra day tour by ferry
breadcrumb: Things to do in Red Sea
Things to do in Sharm el Sheikh

overview.description: Start with pickup from Sharm El Sheikh and travel through the Sinai Peninsula to Taba. From here, take a ferry across the Gulf of Aqaba to Jordan. Make your way to the gorge of Ma'an, where the ancient city of Petra can be found. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Wonders of the World, the city was once described as being "forgotten by the world for over 1,000 years". Petra is home to towering buildings carved into the pink stone. On your tour of the canyon, admire the sight of the Treasure Palace, the Roman Theater, and the Temple and Treasures of the Citadel. One of the most astounding archaeological sites in the world, this tour will allow you to check it off your bucket list. After exploring Petra, enjoy lunch in a local restaurant before heading back to Sharm El Sheikh.

itinerary.description: Pickup and Morning Departure: Your adventure begins with an early morning pickup from your hotel, typically before 7 am. It's recommended to order a Breakfast Box from your hotel to take with you for the journey. You'll be transported to to Dahab, where the day's activities will commence.

Transfer to Dahab and Snorkeling: you'll be taken to the renowned town of Dahab, where an exciting snorkeling experience awaits. Enjoy your complimentary lunch and bring your swim kit, as you'll have the opportunity to take a refreshing dip in the sea. Dahab is known for its fantastic snorkeling opportunities, and you'll have ample time to discover the vibrant underwater world of the Red Sea. Explore Dahab and Local Interaction: your tour may include a stop at the unspoiled town of Dahab. Here, you'll have the chance to engage in some shopping, browse local shops, and interact with the friendly local people. Dahab offers a unique and laid-back atmosphere, making it an ideal place to explore and immerse yourself in the local culture.

Salama Canyon Exploration : after snorkling in dahab you'll be taken to Salama Canyon is a natural wonder characterized by an array of rock formations and crevices, showcasing a mesmerizing display of colors and shapes. Your journey will involve a leisurely walk through the canyon, offering opportunities to marvel at the diverse desert landscapes, barren mountains, sandstone rocks, and a picturesque oasis. During your approximately one-hour walk through the Salama Canyon, you'll have the chance to immerse yourself in the breathtaking scenery and capture the beauty of the desert. Return to Hotel: After an adventurous day of exploring the Salama Canyon, snorkeling, and experiencing Dahab, you'll be transported back to your hotel. Reflect on your day's adventures and cherish the memories of your journey through the captivating landscapes and underwater wonders of the region.

itinerary.description: Sinai mountain & St Catherine Hiking Tour St. Catherine’s Monastery The oldest Christian monastery in the world. The Monastery was built in 337 AD at the place where “God spoke” to all the people the words of the covenant, that is Ten Commandments received by Prophet Moses. The empress of Byzantium Elena, ordered a chapel be established for the pilgrimage of Christians. Emperor Justinian further enlarged the monastery. The Saint Catherine’s Monastery and the Burning Bush began to gain world fame. The monastery was not plundered nor attacked and strands today as a subordinate to the Jerusalem Church. It is one of the UNESCO World Heritage Site. Despite the fact that the monastery of St. Catherine is the smallest diocese in the world. While this is the oldest monastery of the Christian world, which works in our time. The rich history of the monastery has a huge number of icons, ancient manuscripts, priceless of its kind. Mount Sinai Tourists and pilgrims are trying to get to the top of Mount Sinai early in the morning to meet the sunrise, to see from the height, how the sun rises on the horizon and penetrates the clouds. This is an amazing sight that everyone should see once. Therefore, travellers begin their journey in the evening, as the road can take up to 4-5 hours. For an additional fee, we can accommodate local Bedouins and climb Mount Sinai by camel. Tired of traveling, you can refresh yourself with fresh tea and aromatic coffee on the top of a mountain in an old abandoned chapel. There Bedouins sell souvenirs. Christian while making their pilgrimage to the mountain, try to conquer Sinai on foot. Since following religious tradition, this ascent clears them, ennobles the soul and body.

itinerary.description: First visit is Hippodrome . It was the center of sport activities of Constantinople. Famous with 4 monuments; The German Fountain of Wilhelm II, Egyptian Obelisk, Serpentine Column and Column of Constantine.

Haghia Sophia, is the most famous museum in Turkey and one of the greatest marvels of architecture. Haghia Sophia was built as a church in the 6th century by Emperor Justinian then in 1453 renovated into a mosque by Ottoman Emperor Fatih Sultan Mehmet. It was converted into a museum in 1935 and welcoming both local and foreign visitors. (Closed on Monday)

Blue Mosque , as known as the Sultanahmet Mosque, this breath-taking building is one of the most majestic Ottoman Mosques in all of Turkey. Also it was built with unique 6 minarets. (Closed on Friday)

Topkapi Palace, which has been home to the Ottoman dynasty for many years, was used for educational administrative and as the art center of the state. Get knowledge about the imperial treasury sacred islamic relics, palace kitchens and weapons. (Closed on Tuesday)

Grand Bazaar, is the biggest market and the most attractive shopping center of Istanbul which has lots of shopping opportunities with carpets, leather, jewellery, turkish delight, gold, antique tiles etc.. (Closed on Sunday)

One of Istanbul's splendid historical buildings is the Basilica Cistern located in the southwest of Hagia Sophia. This large underground cistern built by Byzantine Emperor Justinian I (527-565) was named as Yerebatan Palace ere among the people due to the marble columns rising from the water and countless seemingly like. It is also known as Basilica Cistern since there is a Basilica in the place where the cistern is located.

overview.description: The 4 Days: 7 Churches of Revelation Tour is a religious tour that visits the seven churches mentioned in the Book of Revelation in the Bible. The tour is usually organized from Izmir or Kusadasi and includes visits to the ancient cities of Ephesus, Pergamum, Thyatira, Smyrna, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. Pick-up and drop-off are typically included in the tour and are provided from Izmir or Kusadasi. However, it is always recommended to confirm with us beforehand. itinerary.description: Welcome to the Izmir Airport. Our tour guide meets you at the Izmir Airport and then you depart from Smyrna. The church at Smyrna suffered amid prosperity for its refusal to devotions the Roman Empire. It was the home of the great second-century Bishop Polycarp who was burned alive at the age of 86.  2 hours • Admission Ticket Included

After Smyrna, we drive to Pergamon, a most memorable experience will be Pergamum with its Acropolis and Great Theatre, Altar of Zeus, and Red Basilica. (Once pagan temple then converted Christian church) Then, we visit Asclepion the famous medical center of Antiquity. At the end of the tour, we go back to Izmir and stay overnight. 3 hours • Admission Ticket Included
After breakfast, we visit of Thyatira which was once a busy trading center. One of the Seven Churches mentioned in Revelations. 2 hours • Admission Ticket Free

Then, you visit to Sardis, coins were minted here. You will be impressed by the massive measure of the Temple of Artemis, Marble Royal Road, Gymnasium, and Synagogue. 2 hours • Admission Ticket Included

Philadelphia is the last visit of the day. Christ told those who overcame that He would write upon them “The name of my god and the name of the city of my God, which is New Jerusalem.” You also see an ancient Wall and Byzantine Basilica. At the end of the tour, you go back to the hotel and stay overnight in Pamukkale.  2 hours • Admission Ticket Included

After breakfast, we go to Pamukkale. Pamukkale is in Aegean Turkey and it is also called the “Cotton Castle”, because of the white cotton appearance of the mineral bath spas that abound the province, which is rich in calcium. Known as a “spa town” since the Roman era, tourists travel to Pamukkale to relax in warm, soothing, and therapeutic waters in the myriad spas. Hierapolis or “Holy City” evangelized by Paul and Epaphras. Also, the Apostle Philip lived and was buried here. What makes Hierapolis different from most places on Earth is that it is built on land, neither on water, but on limestone deposits above the mineral springs in the area. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site because of the ruins that are littered all over the city, including the necropolis that houses the sarcophagi of important ancient figures like Marcus Aurelius. Read less 3 hours • Admission Ticket Included
After lunch break you visit Laodicea, see ruins, stadium and columned streets. At the end of the tour back, you go back to Kusadasi and stay overnight. 1 hour 30 minutes • Admission Ticket Included

In the morning, you will be picked up from your hotel and drive to Ephesus Ancient City. Ephesus was the second-largest city in the Roman Empire over 250.000 people in the 1st BC. Ranking only behind Rome it was the second-largest city in the world. Ephesus was also a harbor city. And, this giant city was built only with marble. Did you know Ephesus had the largest amphitheater in the ancient world over 25.000 seats? Also see Goddess Nike, Local pharmacy, Hadrian Gate, Library of Celsus (the third largest library), Marble Street, and Harbor Street. 3 hours • Admission Ticket Included

The House of Virgin Mary, is located top of the Ephesus and 9 km far away. The places where the Virgin Mary has spent her last days and the Shrine of Virgin Mary pleasures wonderful atmosphere latent in the green. 1 hour • Admission Ticket Included

Basilica of St. John, as early as the 4th or 5th century a Christian church was built over a simple grave, supposedly the grave of St. John. In the 6th century, Emperor Justinian had an impressive domed basilica built to replace the earlier church. At the end of the tour, you will be transferred back to the Izmir Airport. 45 minutes • Admission Ticket Included

itinerary.description: Ephesus, was the second largest city in the Roman Empire over 250.000 people in the 1st BC. Ranking only behind Rome it was the second largest city in the world. Ephesus was also a harbour city. And, this giant city was built only with marbel. Did you know Ephesus had a largest amphitheater in the ancient world over 25.000 seats? Also see Goddess Nike, Local pharmacy, Hadrian Gate, Library of Celcius (the third largest library), Marbel Street and Harbour Street.

A peristyle house on the corner of Curetes Street and the Marble Road is known as the brothel, because in the excavations, a statue of Priapus with an oversize phallus was found in the house. The statue is now presented in Ephesus Museum. The construction of the building dates to the Trajan (98-117 A.D.) It has two entrances, one from the Marble Road and one from the Curetes Street. It has a hall on the first floor , and on the second floor there are number of small rooms. On the west side of the house there is a reception area with colored mosaics on the floor, symbolizing the four season. The chamber next to it is the bath of the house with an elliptical pool. On the floor of the pool, there is a mosaic describing three women eating and drinking, a waitress standing, a mouse and a cat nibbling crumbs.  5 minutes • Admission Ticket Free

Memmius Monument is situated on the north side of the Domitian Square. It was constructed during the reign of Augustus in the 1st century A.D by Memmius, the grand son of dictator Sulla. One can see the figures of his father and grandfather on the blocks today. The structure has four facades, in the 4th century A.D, a square fountain was built on the northwest facade. Dictator Sulla was a hero for the Romans in Ephesus. When the taxes were too high in Ephesus they were fed up with the yoke of Rome.They needed a miracle and it was Mithridates of the Pontic Empire on the Black Sea Coast.His famous motto was ‘Asia for Asiatic’. He killed 80,000 Romans with his army.Three years after his revolt, the Roman army, under the command of Sulla, conquered Mithridates and brought security.This monument was built to remind this conquer in 87BC. 10 minutes • Admission Ticket Free

Located to the south end of the Domitian Street, it is the first structure in Ephesus known to be dedicated to an emperor. It was built on a high and wide terrace set by 50x100 meters in size, on vaulted foundations. The northern size of the terrace seems to be two-stories high, reached by stairs. The stairs are still visible today. The temple, built in pro-style plan, had eight columns on the short side and thirteen columns on the long side, and four additional columns in front of the cella. At the northern side there was an u-shaped altar, which is now displayed in Izmir museum. It was in the reign of Domitian that an emperor gave permission to built an Emperor Temple; that is the permission to be the 'neocoros' for the first time, which was a great honor for a city. When the unpopular emperor was killed by his servant, public quickly took vengeance and erased his name from many inscriptions. Read less 5 minutes • Admission Ticket Free

itinerary.description: Ephesus

In the morning, our tour guide will meet with you at the Kusadasi port. And, we reach to Ephesus. Ephesus, was the second-largest city in the Roman Empire over 250.000 people in the 1st BC. Ranking only behind Rome it was the second-largest city in the world. Ephesus was also a harbor city. And, this giant city was built only with marble. Did you know Ephesus had the largest amphitheater in the ancient world over 25.000 seats? Also see Goddess Nike, Local pharmacy, Hadrian Gate, Library of Celcius (the third largest library), Marble Street, and Harbour Street.
Temple of Artemis or Artemision, also known as the Temple of Diana, was a Greek Temple dedicated to the goddess Artemis. It was located in Ephesus and it was one of the seven wonders of the world.

The House of Virgin Mary, is a place where according to the beliefs of many people Mary, the mother of Jesus, spent her last years of her life. She was supposed to arrive at Ephesus together with St. John and lived there in the years 37-45 CE until her Assumption or Dormition.
Istanbul

You will be picked up from Istanbul Port. Let’s start to explore Istanbul. The first visit is Hippodrome. It was the center of sports activities of Constantinople. Famous with 4 monuments; The German Fountain of Wilhelm II, Egyptian Obelisk, Serpentine Column, and Column of Constantine.

Haghia Sophia, is the most famous museum in Turkey and one of the greatest marvels of architecture. Hagia Sophia was built as a church in the 6th century by Emperor Justinian then in 1453 renovated into a mosque by Ottoman Emperor Fatih Sultan Mehmet. It was converted into a museum in 1935 and welcomed both local and foreign visitors. (Closed on Monday)
Blue Mosque, as known as the Sultanahmet Mosque, this breathtaking building is one of the most majestic Ottoman mosques in all of Turkey. Also, it was built with unique 6 minarets. (Closed on Friday)

Topkapi Palace, which has been home to the Ottoman dynasty for many years, was used for educational administration and as the art center of the state. Get knowledge about the imperial treasury´s sacred Islamic relics, palace kitchens, and weapons. (Closed on Tuesday)

Grand Bazaar, is the biggest market and the most attractive shopping center of Istanbul which has lots of shopping opportunities with carpets, leather, jewelry, Turkish delight, gold, antiquities, etc..(Closed on Sunday)

itinerary.description: Itinerary WHITE DESERT & Black Deserts Over Night Camping – Western Desert The tour begins with pickup from your hotel in Cairo at 7AM and heads out of the city across the surrounding desert landscapes. The first stop of the day is the stunning Bahariya Oasis, which was once the agricultural center during Pharaonic times but is now famous for its abundance of dates and olives. Explore the oasis with your guide and admire the sprawling landscape of shady palms and natural springs. After lunch visit the Black Desert, a fascinating landscape with rugged mountain-like domes that contrast against the sandy surroundings. Next, visit the nearby Agabat, a beautiful valley with imposing white cliff faces and yellow limestone rocks. Follow on to the Crystal Mountain, an incredibly unique formation made entirely of calcite crystal that sparkles and shimmers under the Egyptian sun. Head over to the White Desert next, named for its sprawling white sandy landscape that stretches across the horizon. Climb a number of sand dunes and marvel at the jaw-dropping views that seem to go on forever. As evening draws near, your Bedouin guide will setup camp and prepare a delicious dinner. Enjoy the camp fire, or go for a night stroll before you either sleep under the stars or in a tent. (Sleeping bags can be provided upon request but we always make sure that there is an abundance of blankets in any case). After watching the sun rise in the morning, you will kick start your day with breakfast at the campsite. Afterwards, set off to the Bahariya Oasis to visit the Valley of the Golden Mummies, a large burial site in the Western Desert of Egypt and the Tomb of Bannantiu. overview.description: Private full-day adventure to Fayoum Oasis, located just 95 km south of Cairo. This off-the-beaten-path destination offers a rich blend of history, natural beauty, and thrilling experiences. Your journey begins with a visit to the Museum of Kom Oshim in the village of Kom Oshim, where you'll discover Pharaonic and Roman artifacts, including stunning burial portraits and mummies. Just a short walk away, explore the Karanis Catacombs, one of the largest Greco-Roman burial grounds dating back to the 3rd century BC. Continue your exploration with a stop at the Hawara Pyramid, built by Pharaoh Amenemhat III during the golden age of the Middle Kingdom. Then, relax by Egypt's largest saltwater lake, Qarun Lake, where you can observe waterwheels in motion and spot migratory birds. Enjoy a delicious lunch at a local restaurant, savoring traditional Egyptian cuisine before the adventure takes a thrilling turn. Hop into a 4x4 vehicle for an exciting session of dune bashing and sandboarding on the golden desert dunes. End your day with a visit to the UNESCO World Heritage site of Wadi Hitan, also known as the Valley of the Whales. Here, you'll witness ancient whale fossils over 200 million years old and learn about crucial stages of evolution. Keep an eye out for unique wildlife like the African wildcat and Egyptian mongoose before returning to Cairo.

tour_info.title: Nubian Museum With Philae Temple Private Tour

overview.description: Embark on a journey through time with this private tour of the Nubian Museum and Philae Temple. Explore the fascinating exhibits at the Nubian Museum, showcasing the history and culture of the Nubian people. Learn about their way of life, their art, and the impact of the High Dam construction on their civilization. Afterward, board a motorboat and cruise to Agilika Island, where the magnificent Philae Temple stands. Admire the intricate carvings and reliefs that adorn the temple walls, and discover the stories behind the ancient deities worshipped here. This tour offers a unique opportunity to delve into the past and experience the beauty of ancient Nubia.

itinerary.description: Itinerary Nubian Museum &  Philae Temple Nubian Museum This museum was established in association with UNESCO to preserve the ancient Nubian culture, which was devastated when the Nile was dammed in 1970. The Nubian Museum is one of Aswan’s most fascinating and least-visited attractions. Exhibits run from 6,500 years ago to the present day, from the Kingdom of Kush of the Black Pharaohs to contemporary folk culture. The architecture of the Museum and the enclosure walls are intended to evoke traditional Nubian village architecture, as it was along the Nubian Nile before the region was flooded by Lake Nasser. Your qualified Egyptologist guide will show you some of the most important artifacts before allowing you free time to explore the museum at your leisure. Philae Temple We continue our tour by motorboat to reach Agilika Island, between the old and new Aswan dam, where the Philae Temple is located. The sacred Temple of Isis, this temple is one of Upper Egypt’s most captivating monuments both for the superb artistry of its reliefs and for the striking symmetry of its architecture. The temple was saved by the rising waters of Lake Nasser by UNESCO’s rescue project and moved from its original home on Philae Island to nearby and higher where it sits today.

itinerary.description: Itinerary SIWA OASIS Safari Day 1: Today after having your breakfast at Cairo hotel, you will travel for 300 kilometers north of Cairo for a At first a more somber experience at the historic battle site of El Alamein. It was here that British and Commonwealth soldiers fought a decisive Allied victory against the German Africa Corps that defined the North African campaign. Both sides suffered heavy losses and the memorial commemorates nearly 12,000 Commonwealth servicemen who died in the Western Desert campaigns during the Second World War. Lunch After visiting Al Alamein cemetery, you will drive along the beautiful bay of Marsa Matrouh on the Mediterranean coast where your tasty seafood lunch will be served then you will continue to Siwa Oasis, about 4 hours’ drive from Marsa Matrouh. You are going to start your Safari adventure between the golden sand dunes till we arrive at the fossils area and see the rocky coral reefs which date back to the Cambrian era. Then we will take you to one of the charming sites in the great sand sea a beautiful lake in the middle of the desert, may be you will be lucky enough to see the flamingo birds, you can swim in the cold water of the lake enjoying the calmness of the desert and bathing in a very relaxing atmosphere. Passing by the Dakrour Mountain, a mountain known for its curative climatic properties, especially for Rheumatism patients. As it is famous for the healing properties of its hot sand since ancient times, there Are two cemeteries, one of which is the six columns cut in earlier times and the Greek era Lunch We will stop for lunch in a local restaurant (Vegetarian options are available, kindly indicate during the booking progress) After lunch and to give the day another adrenaline boost. We will enjoy sandboarding experience, although not as fast as snowboarding, but with the right quantity of wax we can let you shoot down some of the extensive sand dunes in the Great Sand Sea and have thrills to spare. After sandboarding it is time to wash up in the hot spring renowned as Bir Wahid for chilling and calming our muscles, enjoy another amazing Sun Set at the Great Sand Sea in the middle of the dunes while having Bedouin tea. itinerary.stop: The Temples of Abu Simbel by Plane
itinerary.description: Temples Abu Simbel Plane The flight from Aswan to the small town of Abu Simbel takes only around 30 minutes. Your Egyptologist guide will accompany you to the famous temples of Ramses II and his favorite wife Nefertari. On the short walk to the temple entrances, your guide will explain the history of the site, including details of the UNESCO-led relocation of the entire cliff face to higher ground, and how the temples were discovered by accident in 1813. Due to the large number of visitors to Abu Simbel, guides are not permitted inside either the Great Temple of Ramses II or the smaller Temple of Hathor. However, by using photos and illustrations, your guide will explain to you the structures and their interior artworks. You will then have free time to enter the temples and explore them at your leisure. As one of the few ancient Egyptian sites which largely escaped damage by past invaders, the interiors of Abu Simbel’s temples are astounding. The scale of the buildings and their detailed decoration leaves most visitors in awe. The temples’ attraction is further enhanced by their scenic location on the edge of Lake Nasser in the orange sands of the desert. After visiting the temples there may be time for a short visit to the small visitor’s center which documents the UNESCO relocation project.

overview.description: Escape the ordinary and embark on a captivating day trip to Luxor, the dazzling jewel of ancient Egypt! Await breathtaking discoveries as you journey from Sharm El Sheikh to Luxor, where history comes alive at every turn. Delve into the legendary Valley of the Kings , a necropolis shrouded in mystery. Descend into the depths of meticulously decorated tombs, each whispering tales of bygone pharaohs and their fascinating burial practices. Your expert Egyptologist guide, available in your preferred language (English, Russian, or Italian), will unravel the secrets of these sacred chambers, bringing the past vividly to life. Continue your adventure to the magnificent Hatshepsut Temple , a marvel of engineering that gracefully scales the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari. Be mesmerized by the temple's unique design and uncover the stories of the powerful female pharaoh who commissioned its creation. Savor a delectable local lunch at a charming Luxor restaurant, fueling your exploration for the afternoon. Prepare to be awestruck by the sheer grandeur of the Karnak Temple Complex , a sprawling masterpiece of ancient architecture. Wander through the vast site, marveling at the iconic Avenue of Sphinxes and the awe-inspiring Hypostyle Hall, its towering pillars reaching towards the heavens. Conclude your day trip with a visit to the Colossi of Memnon , colossal statues that once stood guard at the entrance to a pharaoh's mortuary temple. Capture unforgettable photos against the backdrop of these imposing figures, feeling the weight of history at your fingertips. This whirlwind Luxor adventure, guided in your preferred language (English, Russian, or Italian), is more than just sightseeing - it's a captivating journey through time. Immerse yourself in the rich tapestry of ancient Egyptian culture, from the grandeur of its temples to the captivating stories whispered by the sands of time. Don't miss this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to walk in the footsteps of pharaohs and experience the magic of Luxor

itinerary.description: Hotel Pickup: Your guide will meet you at your hotel in either Cairo or Giza at 8 am or 9 am to begin the day's adventure.

Giza Plateau: The tour starts with a visit to the Giza Plateau, where you'll explore the Pyramids of Giza, including: the Pyramid of Khufu (Cheops), the Pyramid of Khafre (Chephren), the Pyramid of Menkaure (Mycerinus). These ancient pyramids are some of the most famous and well-preserved structures in the world.

3. Sphinx and Valley Temple: After exploring the pyramids, you'll visit the Great Sphinx of Giza, an iconic symbol of ancient Egypt. Adjacent to the pyramids, you'll also explore the Valley Temple, where you can learn about mummification rituals and ancient history.
4. Lunch: Enjoy a traditional Egyptian lunch at a local restaurant, where you can savor authentic dishes and immerse yourself in local cuisine.

5. Egyptian Museum: In the afternoon, you'll proceed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, home to a vast collection of ancient Egyptian artifacts and treasures. One of the highlights of the museum is the exhibit dedicated to King Tutankhamun (Tut Ankh Amon), where you can learn about the mysteries and legends surrounding the "Curse of the Pharaohs."

6. Optional Stops: Depending on your interests and available time, the tour may include optional stops at local bazaars or markets. This allows you to shop for souvenirs or immerse yourself in the local culture.
Hotel Drop-off: At the end of the tour, your guide will safely transfer you back to your hotel in Cairo or Giza, concluding a day filled with history, culture, and exploration.

Your first stop is the renowned Goreme Open-Air Museum, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the ancient rock-cut churches adorned with intricate frescoes that date back to the Byzantine era. itinerary.description: The tour begins with a pick-up from your hotel in Izmir by your tour guide.
Upon arrival, you'll be greeted by the impressive ruins of Pergamon, an ancient Greek and Roman city known for its rich history, stunning architecture, and cultural heritage.

The tour begins with a visit to the Pergamon Acropolis, perched atop a hill overlooking the modern town of Bergama. Highlights of the Acropolis include the imposing Temple of Trajan, the monumental Altar of Zeus, the ancient theater, and the library complex.

After exploring the Acropolis, you'll continue your journey to the Asclepion of Pergamon, an ancient medical center dedicated to the Greek god of healing, Asclepius. Explore the ruins of this sacred site, which includes temples, baths, a theater, and the renowned Temple of Asclepius.

itinerary.description: Ephesus, was the second largest city in the Roman Empire over 250.000 people in the 1st BC. Ranking only behind Rome it was the second largest city in the world. Ephesus was also a harbour city. And, this giant city was built only with marbel. Did you know Ephesus had a largest amphitheater in the ancient world over 25.000 seats? Also see Goddess Nike, Local pharmacy, Hadrian Gate, Library of Celcius (the third largest library), Marbel Street and Harbour Street.

Terraced Houses, are located on the hill, opposite the Hadrian Temple. Also called as “the houses of rich”, they are important for the reason that they give us an idea about the family life during the Roman period. They were built according to Hippodamian plan of the city in which roads transected each other of right angles.

St. John Basilica, was a basilica in Ephesus. It was constructed by Justinian I in the 6th Century. It stands over the believed burial site of John the Apostle. It was modeled after the now last Church of the Holy Apostles in Constantinople.

The House of Virgin Mary, is a place where according to the beliefs of many people Mary, the mother of Jesus, spent her last years of her life. She was supposed to arrive at Ephesus together with St. John and lived there in the years 37-45 CE until her Assumption or Dormition.

itinerary.description: Itinerary Luxor By Bus We will start our trip by driving to Luxor in an air-conditioned vehicle to visit Thebes, the famous ancient capital of Egypt.  Karnak Temple Karnak is an extraordinary complex of sanctuaries, kiosks, pylons and obelisks dedicated to the Theban triad but also to the greater glory of pharaohs. The site covers more than 2 sq km; it’s large enough to contain about 10 cathedrals and is considered the largest temple complex in the world. At its heart is the Temple of Amun, the earthly ‘home’ of the local god. Built, added to, dismantled, restored, enlarged and decorated over nearly 1500 years, Karnak was the most important place of worship in Egypt during the New Kingdom. Lunch We will recharge our batteries by stopping for lunch in a local restaurant on the west bank of the Nile. Temple of Queen Hatshepsut Leaving the hot sands of the Valley of the Kings, you will visit the Temple of Hatshepsut, one of the most striking monuments in Egypt. Your guide will introduce you to the history of the temple and the story of Queen Hatshepsut, the famous female ruler of Egypt who posed as a male to gain the throne. There is free time to explore at your leisure as you wander the large courtyards and admire the intricate hieroglyphic decorations Colossi of Memnon The two faceless Colossi of Memnon, originally representing Pharaoh Amenhotep III, rising majestically about 18m from the plain, are the first monuments tourists see when they visit the west bank. tour_info.title: Unearthing Pharaoh’s Legacy: A Camping Adventure to Serabit

overview.description: Unearthing Pharaoh’s Legacy: A Camping Adventure to Serabit Serabit al Khadem is a locality in the southwest Sinai Peninsula where copper and turquoise were mined extensively in antiquity, mainly by the ancient Egyptians. Archaeological excavation, initiated by Flinders Petrie at the beginning of the 19th century revealed ancient mining camps and a long-lived temple dedicated to Hathor, the Egyptian goddess who was considered the protector in desert regions of the mine workers. Hathor was also referred as the Turquoise Lady. The temple, located at an altitude of 850 m above sea level is about 10 km north of Wadi Maghara and about 43 km east of Abu Zenima , is one of the most important temples of ancient Egypt. It was built during the XII Dynasty (1955- 1750 BC) by the miners ruled by the Pharaoh Snefru, however it seems that mining activity can be dated back to the III Dynasty (2670-2570 BC) and continued at least after the XVIII Dynasty (1550 to 1292 BC). During this period Queen Hat-Shep-Sut and her stepson Tuthmosi III built the lower part of the Temple of Serabit and ordered to engrave numerous votive steles that are still visible. In ancient times the Temple was also known as a place of worship and healing, as evidenced by the many votive steles found in the temple and in the cave. Serabit el Khadem means “Columns of the Slave” and refers to the tall votive steles that dominate the ruins of the ancient Egyptian temple. The temple was built on a plateau and extends for about two thousand squares meters starting from a cave cut in the rocks dedicated as well to the goddess Hathor. A detailed description of the temple and the Serabit al Khadem area is given by Alberto Siliotti in his book: Guide to Exploration of the Sinai Close to the temple to the North the entrance of the old mines are visible.

This captivating journey isn't just about the sights; it's about immersing yourself in the soul of the Sinai. By the time we return you to your hotel, you'll carry within you the unforgettable memories of a desert adventure unlike any other.

tour_info.title: The Temples of Abu Simbel by Bus From Aswan

overview.description: Experience the grandeur of ancient Egypt on a day tour from Aswan to the temples of Abu Simbel. Journey through the desert landscape to reach these awe-inspiring rock-cut temples, originally carved into the cliff face and later relocated to higher ground to protect them from rising lake levels. Upon arrival, explore the Great Temple of Ramses II, a colossal structure adorned with intricate carvings and statues. Discover the smaller Temple of Hathor, dedicated to the goddess of love and joy. Your knowledgeable guide will share fascinating insights into the history, architecture, and symbolism of these magnificent monuments. Enjoy the opportunity to take photos and soak in the breathtaking beauty of the temples. Afterward, visit the visitor center to learn more about the UNESCO relocation project and see related exhibits. As you make your return journey to Aswan, reflect on the incredible experience of witnessing these ancient wonders and gaining a deeper appreciation for Egypt's rich heritage.

itinerary.stop: The Temples of Abu Simbel by Bus From Aswan
itinerary.description: Itinerary Temples Abu Simbel Bus Depart Aswan to journey 280 kilometers to the stunning rock-carved temples of Abu Simbel. Relocated to the west banks of Lake Nasser, the temple complex is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of the “Nubian Monuments.” On arrival, take a short walk to the temple entrance, where your Egyptologist guide will explain the history of the site. Hear details of the UNESCO-led relocation of the entire cliff face to higher ground, and how the temples were only discovered by accident in 1813. Due to the large number of visitors, guides are not permitted inside the Great Temple of Ramses II or the smaller Temple of Hathor. However, by using photos and illustrations your guide will explain the structures and their interior artworks before giving you some free time to enter the temples and explore at leisure. As one of the few Ancient Egyptian sites that largely escaped damage from past invaders, the interiors of the Abu Simbel temples are astounding. The scale of the buildings and their detailed decorations leave most visitors in awe. The experience is further enhanced by the scenic location on the edge of Lake Nasser in the orange sands of the desert. After visiting the temples, benefit from some time for a short visit to the small visitor’s center to see documents relating to the UNESCO relocation before the drive back to Aswan.

tour_info.title: Half Day Private: Kalabsha Temple

overview.description: Half Day Private: Kalabsha Temple Tour Embark on a captivating journey to the ancient Kalabsha Temple, a remarkable example of Nubian temple architecture. Originally built by Roman emperor Octavius Augustus, the temple was relocated to its current location on Lake Nasser in the 1960s to preserve it from rising floodwaters. As you explore the temple, marvel at the impressive stone causeway leading to the first pylon. Step into the colonnaded court and the grand hypostyle hall, adorned with towering columns and intricate inscriptions. Discover the sanctuary, consisting of three chambers, and climb to the rooftop for breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape. With its well-preserved structures and rich history, Kalabsha Temple offers a fascinating glimpse into the ancient world. Join us on this unforgettable tour and experience the grandeur of this iconic Nubian monument.

itinerary.description: Half Day Kalabsha Temple Kalabsha Temple We will drive through the daily life of Aswan city to get to the stunning waterfront temple. Originally built in 30 BC by Roman emperor Octavius Augustus, in the 1960s after the building of the Aswan High Dam, the temple was dismantled and relocated here. During your visit you can view the impressive stone causeway leading from the lake to the first pylon of the temple, beyond which are the colonnaded court and the great hypostyle hall. Inscriptions on the walls show various emperors and pharaohs in the presence of gods and goddesses. Just beyond the hall is the sanctuary, consisting of three chambers. Stairs from one chamber lead up to the roof, from where you can take in superb views of Lake Nasser and the High Dam. tour_info.title: Private Old Virgin Canyon: Unveiling the Secrets of Sinai

overview.description: Craving an adventure beyond the beach? This private Sinai Desert safari is your portal to a bygone era. Buckle up in a comfortable jeep and let our expert guide whisk you away on a journey unlike any other. As the desert unfolds before you, imagine yourself traversing ancient trade routes, the wind whispering tales of the past. Our first stop is the magnificent Old Virgin's Canyon, a geological marvel carved by eons of wind and sand. Towering rock walls, sculpted into mesmerizing shapes, will leave you breathless. Unveil the secrets held within these canyons, from rare desert flora to the fascinating history of the Nawamis, ancient one-person shelters. But the adventure doesn't stop there! Embrace your inner explorer and conquer the slopes of Hadudha Mountain on a thrilling sandboarding escapade. Feel the rush of adrenaline as you race down the golden dunes, the vast desert stretching out before you. Next, channel your inner Indiana Jones and embark on a majestic camel ride through the heart of the desert. Let the rhythmic gait of your camel lull you into a sense of timeless serenity as you soak in the breathtaking scenery. As the day progresses, indulge in a delicious Bedouin feast, a symphony of flavors prepared fresh in the heart of the canyons. Savor the warmth of Bedouin hospitality as you sip on aromatic coffee and tea brewed over a traditional open fire. This captivating journey isn't just about the sights; it's about immersing yourself in the soul of the Sinai. By the time we return you to your hotel, you'll carry within you the unforgettable memories of a desert adventure unlike any other.

overview.description: Experience the grandeur of ancient Egypt on a day tour from Aswan to the temples of Abu Simbel. itinerary.stop: The Temples of Abu Simbel by Bus From Aswan
itinerary.description: Itinerary Temples Abu Simbel Bus Depart Aswan to journey 280 kilometers to the stunning rock-carved temples of Abu Simbel. Relocated to the west banks of Lake Nasser, the temple complex is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of the “Nubian Monuments.” On arrival, take a short walk to the temple entrance, where your Egyptologist guide will explain the history of the site. Hear details of the UNESCO-led relocation of the entire cliff face to higher ground, and how the temples were only discovered by accident in 1813. Due to the large number of visitors, guides are not permitted inside the Great Temple of Ramses II or the smaller Temple of Hathor. However, by using photos and illustrations your guide will explain the structures and their interior artworks before giving you some free time to enter the temples and explore at leisure. As one of the few Ancient Egyptian sites that largely escaped damage from past invaders, the interiors of the Abu Simbel temples are astounding. The scale of the buildings and their detailed decorations leave most visitors in awe. The experience is further enhanced by the scenic location on the edge of Lake Nasser in the orange sands of the desert. After visiting the temples, benefit from some time for a short visit to the small visitor’s center to see documents relating to the UNESCO relocation before the drive back to Aswan.

Lunch Break: Savor a delicious lunch and refreshing drinks on board the boat. Afternoon Dives: Depending on weather conditions, you may have additional practice dives or free time for snorkeling (equipment permitting). Return to Sharm El Sheikh: Relax on the boat ride back to the shore, where transportation will be waiting to take you back to your hotel. Day 4: Explore More or Dive Deeper (Ras Mohamed or Tiran Island) Morning: Pick-up from your hotel and transfer to the boat by air-conditioned vehicle. Dive Choice: Depending on weather and your progress, you'll either head back to Ras Mohamed or venture further to Tiran Island, renowned for its vibrant coral reefs. The Grand Finale: Complete two more open water dives, solidifying your newfound skills and exploring the underwater wonders of the Red Sea. Lunch Break: Enjoy another delicious meal and refreshments on board. Certification Confirmation: Your instructor will confirm your PADI reference number, allowing you to receive a temporary license upon returning to shore. Return to Hotel: Relax on the boat ride back and get transferred back to your hotel in Sharm El Sheikh. (Your permanent PADI license will be mailed to your home address) Points of Interest: Sharm El Sheikh: Bustling resort town serving as your base for the diving adventure. Ras Mohamed National Park: Renowned for its diverse marine life, coral reefs, and shipwrecks. (Potential dive site) Tiran Island: A remote island offering exceptional coral formations and a chance encounter with pelagic creatures. (Potential dive site, depending on weather conditions) Red Sea: Experience the crystal-clear waters teeming with vibrant coral reefs, colorful fish, and other marine life.

additional_info: Health and Physical Requirements: To ensure your safety and enjoyment, some health restrictions apply for scuba diving. overview.description: Embark on a captivating journey through Cairo's rich history and vibrant culture. This full-day tour offers a comprehensive experience, starting with a visit to the world-famous Pyramids of Giza. Marvel at the colossal structures and learn about their construction and significance. Continue to the enigmatic Sphinx, a majestic guardian of the pyramids. Next, delve into the treasures of the Egyptian Museum, home to an impressive collection of artifacts spanning millennia. Conclude your day with a visit to the bustling Khan el Khalili Bazaar, a vibrant marketplace filled with colorful shops and stalls. Immerse yourself in the lively atmosphere, haggle for souvenirs, and experience the authentic Egyptian culture. This tour provides a unique opportunity to witness the beauty and history of Cairo in a single day. With expert guidance and comfortable transportation, you'll create unforgettable memories.

itinerary.description: Itinerary Pyramids Sphinx Egyptian Museum Bazaar Egyptian Museum Start your tour at the Egyptian Museum. Designed by the French architect Marcel Dourgnon, the museum is located in a handsome neo-classical building on famous Tahrir Square. Its collections exceed 120,000 masterpieces, ranging from the pre-dynastic era, to the Pharaonic and Greco-Roman periods. Undoubted highlights are the collection of rare treasures of King Tutankhamen, and the Mummies Room, which you can enter for a small extra charge. 1 -Pyramids of Giza Pyramids Sphinx Egyptian Museum Bazaar Continue to the Great Pyramids of Giza and Great Sphinx, the oldest of the 7 Wonders of the Ancient World, and the last still standing. Explore the Pyramids of Cheops, Chephren, and Mykerinos. Your guide will describe the story of their monumental construction, and tell you about their mysteries, before you explore inside one of the pyramids (to enter inside the Cheops and Chephren pyramids an additional optional ticket is needed, your guide will remind you, or you can choose to add it during the booking process). 2 -Sphinx & Valley Temple Pyramids Sphinx Egyptian Museum Bazaar Proceed to the Great Sphinx, imposingly standing in the desert sand after thousands of years. Admire the colossal structure, before moving to the Valley Temple of King Chephren. 3 -Lunch Khan el Khalili Bazaar Drive back to central Cairo and end your day at the lively Khan El Khalili Bazaar. Master the art of bargaining for great prices on fine brassware, copper, perfumes, leather, silver, gold, and antiques.

overview.description: This full-day excursion takes you to Pamukkale's natural wonder and the ancient city of Hierapolis. Once you arrive at Pamukkale, you will have the opportunity to explore the stunning terraced travertine pools and the ancient ruins of Hierapolis. itinerary.description: Ephesus , was the second largest city in the Roman Empire over 250.000 people in the 1st BC. Ranking only behind Rome it was the second largest city in the world. Ephesus was the harbour city. This giant city was built only with marbel. Did you know Ephesus had a largest amphitheater in the ancient world over 25.000 seats. Also see Goddess Nike, Local pharmacy, Hadrian Gate, Library of Celcius (the third largest library), Marbel Street, Harbour Street.

Ephesus Museum , this fascinating Ephesus Museum houses the statues of Ephesian Artemis which are found from the Temple of Artemis, Eros Statues, Hall of the Roman Empires, the Carvings of Hadrian Temple, biblical inscriptions statue of Dormition and the statues of Augustus and Livia.

Terraced Houses , are located on the hill, opposite the Hadrian Temple. Also called as “the houses of rich”, they are important for the reason that they give us an idea about the family life during the Roman period. They were built according to Hippodamian plan of the city in which roads transected each other of right angles.

The House of Virgin Mary , is a place where according to the beliefs of many people Mary, the mother of Jesus, spent her last years of her life. She was supposed to arrive at Ephesus together with St. John and lived there in the years 37-45 CE until her Assumption or Dormition.

tour_info.title: Spectacular Pergamon & Asceplion Tour From Kusadasi & Selcuk Hotels

overview.description: the Spectacular Pergamon & Asclepion Tour from Kusadasi & Selcuk Hotels is a full-day tour that takes you to two of the most impressive ancient sites in Turkey. The tour will start with a pick-up from your hotel in Kusadasi or Selcuk in the morning. Then, you'll be driven to Pergamon, which is located about 1.5 hours away. Once you arrive, your guide will take you on a walking tour of the ancient city and show you its most important landmarks, including the Altar of Zeus, the Theatre, the Library, the Temple of Athena, and the Gymnasium. After exploring Pergamon, you'll head to the nearby Asclepion, an ancient healing center dedicated to the god of medicine, Asclepius. Here, you'll learn about the site's history and see the remains of the medical facilities, including the Roman baths, the temple of Asclepius, and the underground passageways. At the end of the tour, you'll be driven back to your hotel in Kusadasi or Selcuk.

itinerary.description: Your guide and driver will pick you up and then journey to Pergamon. You will visit the breathtaking Acropolis, which was modelled after the site in Athens. The beautiful view from the hill-top will give you a great panorama of the surroundings. Marvel at the impressive Athenaeum library once held 200,000 volumes, which Mark Antony later offered to Cleopatra as a wedding present. The Temple of Trojan is a huge marble building that has been partially reconstructed from the original pieces found on the site.

Following on from this you will discover the famous Sanctuary of Asclepius , located down in the valley from the Acropolis. A sacred fountain where people with health problems could bathe can be found here and legend has it that Asclepius would then give them a vision and explain how they could be cured. After a delicious lunch with Turkish specialities, you will have the opportunity to visit the Archeological Museum of Pergamon where you can see many original artefacts found on the site. At the end of the day, we will enjoy an easy drive through the countryside. Please note that your tour may change the order in which you visit sites.

itinerary.description: Hippodrome. It was the center of sport activities of Constantinople. Famous with 4 monuments, The German Fountain of Wilhelm II, Egyptian Obelisk, Serpentine Column, Column of Constantine.

Haghia Sophia, is the most famous museum in Turkey and one of the greatest marvels of architecture. Haghia Sophia was built as a church in the 6th century by Emperor Justinian then in 1453 renovated into a mosuqe by Ottoman Emperor Fatih Sultan Mehmet. It was converted into a museum in 1935 and welcoming both local and foreign visitors. (Closed on Monday)
Blue Mosque, as known as the Sultanahmet Mosque, this breath-taking building is one of the most majestic Ottoman Mosques in all of Turkey. Also it was built with unique 6 minarets. (Closed on Friday)

Topkapi Palace, which has been home to the Ottoman dynasty for many years, was used educational administrative and art center of state. Get knowledge about the imperial treasury sacred islamic relics, palace kitchens, weapons. (Closed on Tuesday)

Grand Bazaar, is the biggest market and the most attractive shopping center of Istanbul which has lots of shopping oppurtunities with carpets, leather, jewellery, turkish delight, gold, antique tiles etc.. (Closed on Sunday)
